WHAT WE ARRANGE FOR YOU

We start from what you already have.

Not every customer needs a new treatment plant. First we assess the existing solution and its technical potential.

Technology assessment

Establishing the condition of the current WWTP and the parts that need attention.

Modernisation design

Defining suitable modifications and related works for the specific plant.

Replacements and additions

Renewal of the technological equipment and related components.

Optimisation and capacity upgrades

Options for changing the operation or upgrading capacity are assessed for each specific WWTP.

A CLEAR SEQUENCE OF STEPS

Assessment first. Then the design.

The scope of the refurbishment and the achievable parameters depend on the actual condition of the plant and its operating conditions.

  1. 01

    Existing condition

    We discuss the current technology, how it is operated and the reason for the planned change.

  2. 02

    Renewal options

    We assess modifications, additions, equipment replacements and modernisation options.

  3. 03

    Specific scope

    We propose a technical solution that matches the condition we have found.

  4. 04

    Implementation and operation

    The agreed works can be followed by commissioning, operator training and servicing.

BEFORE YOU GET IN TOUCH

What you may want to know.

Do you have a specific installation or brief? Let's go through it together.

+420 736 403 795
Does an older WWTP always have to be replaced completely?+

Not always. In some cases, part of the plant can be retained and the technology renewed. The right approach depends on the technical condition and the needs of the operation.

What can a refurbishment include?+

A technology assessment, modernisation design, replacement or addition of equipment, optimisation of operation and, where possible, a capacity upgrade of the existing treatment plant.

Can the new operating parameters be determined in advance?+

Specific parameters have to be assessed according to the condition of the plant, the proposed technology and the operating conditions. A refurbishment in itself therefore does not automatically mean increased capacity or any other predetermined parameters.
